title: Design and Implementation of Primary Care Interventions Supporting Environmental Health Co-Benefits According to the PRISM-RE-AIM Framework
official: Design and Implementation of a Series of Primary Care Interventions Supporting Environmental Health Co-Benefits According to the PRISM-RE-AIM Methodological Framework
summary:
Environmental changes represent a major threat to human health by affecting access to water, food security, and air quality. They contribute to the increasing burden of communicable and non-communicable diseases, mental health disorders, and premature mortality. The concept of Planetary Health recognizes the interdependence between human health and ecosystems and highlights the principle of co-benefits, whereby certain interventions simultaneously improve individual health and environmental health.

Within this context, the "12 Months, 12 Actions" project, initially developed in Switzerland, consists of an awareness-raising campaign delivering monthly practical messages aimed at promoting behaviors that benefit both health and the environment. This initiative has already received recognition and has been piloted in primary care settings. Previous experiences have demonstrated (i) its feasibility and (ii) its potential to support health-promoting and environmentally sustainable behaviors. However, its actual impact on behavioral outcomes remains to be evaluated.

The present study aims to implement and evaluate this project in France by focusing on two priority actions because of their potential to improve individual health, public health, and environmental health: reducing meat consumption and promoting physical activity. Despite the importance of these issues, no implementation strategies have yet demonstrated proven effectiveness in primary care settings.

Drawing upon Implementation Science and the PRISM-REAIM framework (Practical, Robust Implementation and Sustainability Model - Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation, and Maintenance), the investigators aim to design, test, and implement innovative interventions based on Social Psychology and Social Marketing principles. The study seeks to demonstrate the feasibility of implementing these interventions, the feasibility of assessing their effectiveness, and their potential transferability to other primary care settings.

The project adopts a complex study design structured into four sequential phases, each corresponding to one of the study objectives and guided by appropriate methodological frameworks.

* Phase 1 - Primary Objective: Contextual Analysis Using the PRISM Framework
* Healthcare professionals component: convergent parallel mixed-methods design combining qualitative and quantitative approaches.
* Participants component: explanatory sequential mixed-methods design combining qualitative and quantitative approaches.
* Phase 2 - Secondary Objective A: Integration of findings from both components of the contextual analysis, followed by the development of interventions to be implemented in France. These interventions will be adapted from preliminary intervention prototypes previously developed in Switzerland, together with the design of an implementation plan.
* Phase 3 - Secondary Objective B: Implementation of the intervention implementation plan and preparation of the intervention evaluation process. This phase will follow an iterative process based on (i) interactions within the Steering Committee (COPIL - Comité de Pilotage, Steering Committee) and (ii) interactions between the Steering Committee and participating teams responsible for implementing the interventions within their primary care organizations. An Agile Project Management methodology will be used, relying on an incremental and flexible approach that incorporates continuous testing, rapid feedback, and iterative adaptation.
* Phase 4 - Secondary Objective C: Multi-method pilot study of data collection procedures, including an evaluation of both implementation outcomes and intervention effectiveness using the RE-AIM framework

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria :

Healthcare Professionals

* Primary care professional
* Self-employed or salaried
* Clinical or non-clinical role
* Practicing within a participating primary care office, pharmacy, multidisciplinary primary care center, or Territorial Professional Health Community (Communauté Professionnelle Territoriale de Santé \[CPTS\])
* Informed about the study
* Willing to participate in the study Adult Participants
* Adult (≥18 years old)
* Routinely receiving care within a participating primary care organization
* French language proficiency equivalent to at least level A2 of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR)
* No objection to data collection
* Willing to participate in the study

Exclusion Criteria :

Exclusion Criteria for Adult Participants

* Cognitive impairment limiting the ability to understand study information and procedures
* Participant under legal protection or guardianship Additional Exclusion Criteria for Participants Recruited in the Pilot Study (Phase 4 - RE-AIM Evaluation)
* Previous exposure to the intervention prior to study inclusion
* Consultation within the participating organization between intervention implementation and participant recruitment.
